nameStory: The hepatic tanager gets its name from its rich, liver-red coloration, as 'hepatic' comes from the Greek word for liver. This deep reddish-brown plumage sets it apart from its brighter red cousins like the scarlet and summer tanagers.
description: The hepatic tanager is a medium-sized songbird about the size of a robin, with a sturdy build and thick, pale bill. Males display deep brick-red or liver-colored plumage, while females are more subdued with olive-yellow tones. This western species is an extremely rare visitor to New England, making any sighting a true birding treasure. They're part of the cardinal family despite their tanager name.

idTips.label: Male coloration
idTips.description: Deep brick-red or liver-red plumage, darker and more brownish than the brilliant red of scarlet tanagers

idTips.label: Bill shape
idTips.description: Thick, pale grayish or horn-colored bill that looks sturdy and conical, noticeably different from the darker bills of other tanagers

idTips.label: Size and build
idTips.description: Stockier and more robust than scarlet tanagers, with a slightly heavier appearance and broader chest

idTips.label: Female appearance
idTips.description: Olive-yellow with grayish wash, more subdued than female summer tanagers and with the same pale, thick bill as males

idTips.label: Voice
idTips.description: Song resembles a robin's but with a hoarser, scratchier quality, like a robin with a sore throat

habitat: In their western range, hepatic tanagers prefer pine-oak woodlands and mountain forests. Any New England sightings would likely be in mixed woodlands or parks during migration, possibly attracted to fruiting trees or backyard feeders.

seasonality.spring: Extremely rare vagrant during spring migration in May. Any sighting would likely be of a lost bird far from its normal western range.
seasonality.summer: Not expected in New England during breeding season, as they nest in western mountain forests. Any summer record would be extraordinary.
seasonality.fall: Slightly more likely during fall migration from August through October, when birds occasionally wander east of their normal range.
seasonality.winter: Not present in New England winters, as they migrate to Central America or remain in warmer parts of their western range.

funFact: Despite being called tanagers for over a century, hepatic tanagers were recently reclassified into the cardinal family based on DNA studies - making them more closely related to your backyard cardinals than to the tropical tanagers they were named after!
confusionNotes: Most likely confused with scarlet tanager males, but hepatic tanagers have much darker, brownish-red plumage (think liver vs. fire engine) and pale bills instead of dark ones. Remember: 'Hepatic has a hefty, pale bill.'
contextualKnowledge: The recent reclassification from the tanager family to the cardinal family reflects how DNA analysis has revolutionized bird taxonomy. Many 'tanagers' in North America turned out to be cardinals in disguise, while true tanagers are mostly tropical birds.
compareHints: Hepatic tanagers are much darker red than scarlet tanagers and have pale bills versus dark bills. They're stockier than summer tanagers and lack the yellow-green wing bars of western tanagers. The brick-red color and robust build with pale bill make hepatic tanagers unique among the Piranga genus.

relatedSpecies.distinction: Scarlet tanagers are the only Piranga tanager regularly found in New England, though summer tanagers occasionally wander north.
Western Tanagers are easily distinguished from Scarlet Tanagers by their yellow (not red) bodies and prominent white wing bars.
Summer tanagers are the only all-red Piranga tanager - scarlet tanagers have black wings and tails, while western tanagers show yellow and black markings.
